findings.claim: Status now returns partial whenever the "agent" key is missing. A user who installed hooks before this change (hooks owned, no agent key) or whose install failed to write the key now sees status partial; the 'sync check' (SyncCheck calls Status) also turns partial for previously healthy installs. The message tells them to run install-hooks, so this is the intended behavior, but SyncCheck consumers that treat non-supported as failure regress on previously valid installs.

In mainAgentStatus, an error from InspectMainAgent is reported as CapabilityUnsupported, while the hooks Inspect error path for the same unreadable/malformed file is reported differently (the existing test pins malformed settings as a failure of status). Inconsistent status class for the same cause; also InspectMainAgent re-reads and re-parses the file a second time, so a file changed between the two reads yields a mixed verdict.

foreignAgentNotice is built by re-inspecting the file after Install/Update; an inspect error is silently swallowed and the notice dropped, so install reports restart_required without the notice if the re-read fails. The optional-interface type assertion also means a wrapped or different installer silently skips the key check with no signal, making status say 'supported' while the foreman is not enabled.

ForeignMainAgentNotice formats the key with a hand-written "%s" quote and the value with %q, mixing quoting styles; the notice for the key name is not escaped the same way as the value, and the runtime status messages duplicate the wording by string concatenation rather than a shared builder, so the three texts can drift.

evidence: Read the full diff; the runtime adapter now consults an optional MainAgentInspector for Status, Install and Update.
Status path: hooks owned check first, then mainAgentStatus returns partial for missing or conflicting key; previously the same state returned supported.
The capability declaration lists three new tests that exist in claude_main_agent_test.go.
